stem.en: A grower plants a cutting with all its leaves still on, so the lower leaves end up under the soil. What is likely to go wrong?

text.en: The cutting will make seeds in place of roots.

feedback.en: A stem cutting does not make seeds in place of roots.

text.en: The buried leaves will rot in the damp soil.

feedback.en: Yes. Leaves under the soil rot, which is why the lower leaves come off first.

text.en: The upper leaves will fall off in a single day.

feedback.en: Nothing here makes the upper leaves fall. The fault is under the soil.

text.en: The cutting will turn into a different variety.

feedback.en: A cutting stays the same variety as its parent, whatever is done to its leaves.

explanation.en: The lower leaves are removed because they would be buried, and buried leaves rot. The upper leaves stay on the cutting.

hints.en: What happens to a leaf kept in damp soil?
Which leaves does the gardener remove first?
